q: 1. The least count of a vernier scale is
options: sum of the smallest division of main and vernier scales
value of one division of the primary scale divided by total number of divisions of vernier scale
value of one division of vernire scale divided by total number of division of primary scale
explain: Least count of a vernier = (value of one main scale division) / (total number of divisions on the vernier scale); this is the smallest reading directly obtainable with the vernier.

q: 2. Intersection is preferred to radiation when ...............
options: it is not possible to measure any distance
the points are too far and invisible
explain: The intersection method locates points by the crossing of two rays from different stations, eliminating the need to measure distance to the point physically.

q: 3. An advantage of plane tabling is ...............
options: changes to miss details are less
explain: Because plotting happens in the field while looking at the terrain, the surveyor is less likely to omit important details.

q: 4. While surveying a plot of land by Plane tabling, the field observations
options: and plotting do not proceed simultaneously
and recorded in field books to be plotted later
explain: The key characteristic of plane table surveying is that field observation and plotting are done together at the same time in the field, unlike other methods where plotting is done later in the office.

q: 5. The instrument which is used in plane tabling for obtaining horizontal and vertical distances directly without resorting to chaining, is known as
explain: A telescopic alidade fitted with stadia hairs allows horizontal and vertical distances to be read directly (by tacheometric principles) without chaining, unlike a plain alidade which is only a sighting/ruling device.

q: 6. Plotting of inaccessible points on a plane table, is done by
explain: Inaccessible points (points that cannot be reached to measure distance) are plotted by the method of intersection, sighting the point from two known plane table stations and drawing rays to fix its position.

q: 7. Locating the position of a plane table station with reference to three known points, is known as
explain: The three-point problem is the specific technique of orienting a plane table and fixing the instrument's own station by resection with reference to three known, plotted points.

q: 8. Pick up the method of surveying in which field observations and plotting proceed simultaneously from the following
explain: Plane table surveying is unique in that field observation and plotting are carried out together at the same time in the field.

q: 9. Which one of the following procedures for getting accurate orientation is the most distinctive feature of the art of plane tabling
explain: Resection (particularly the two-point and three-point problems) is considered the most distinctive and skill-demanding feature of plane table surveying, used to orient the table accurately.

q: 10. Methods adopted for traversing are
options: chain traversing and loose needle method
chain angle method and fast needle method
explain: Traversing can be done using various methods such as 'loose needle' (compass), 'fast needle' (theodolite), or by measuring angles between lines using a chain.

q: 11. The technique of plotting all the accessible stations with a single set up of plane table is called
explain: Radiation is the method in which rays are drawn from a single plane table station to each visible (accessible) point, and distances are plotted to scale along these rays, all from one setup.

q: 12. Radiation plane table survey is the best suited when
explain: Radiation requires measuring the actual distance from the instrument station to each point, so it is best suited when the points are both close by and physically accessible for chaining.

q: 13. An advantage of plane tabling is
options: chances to miss details are less.
explain: Because plotting is done in the field itself while the ground is in view, there is little chance of any topographic detail being missed, which is a key advantage of plane table surveying.

q: 14. The 'fix' of a plane table station with three known points, is bad if the plane station lies
options: on the circumference of the circumscribing circle
explain: If the station lies on the circle passing through the three control points (the great circle), the position is indeterminate because all points on that arc will satisfy the angular conditions.

q: 15. To orient a plane table at a point with two inaccessible points, the method generally adopted, is
explain: The Two-Point Problem is a resection method used to orient the table when only two points are known and available for sighting, but are not necessarily accessible.

q: 16. Accuracy of 'fix' by two point problem, is
explain: The two-point problem is generally considered less accurate and less reliable than the three-point problem due to the lack of a third check-line to confirm the position.

q: 17. The process of putting the plane table into some fixed position so that a line representing certain direction of the plane is parallel to the direction in the field is known as
explain: Orientation is the process of aligning the plane table so that lines drawn on the sheet are parallel to the corresponding lines/directions on the ground.

q: 18. Which one of the following is known as instrumental error in plane table surveying?
explain: Non-horizontality of the plane table board is an instrumental (equipment set-up) error, as distinct from personal errors like defective sighting, orientation, or centering.

q: 19. Accurate centering of a plane table is done by
explain: A plumbing fork (with a plumb bob) is the instrument used to accurately centre the plane table exactly over the ground station point.

q: 20. The working edge of an alidade, is known as
explain: The straight ruling edge of an alidade against which sighting/drawing lines are drawn is specifically called the fiducial edge.

q: 21. In the method of plane table survey the object to be plotted is sighted from two plane table stations. This method is called as
explain: Sighting the same object from two different, known plane table stations and plotting its position at the intersection of the two resulting rays is the method of intersection.

q: 22. While plane tabling in plane and open area, the most important operation for setting up the plane table is
explain: Orientation is the process of keeping the table parallel to the positions it occupied at previous stations, ensuring the map remains geographically consistent.

q: 23. Finding the location of the station occupied by the table, on the sheet by means of sighting to three well defined points whose locations have been previously plotted on the sheet, is known as
explain: This specific technique of locating the occupied plane table station using three known, already-plotted points is called the three-point problem.

q: 24. The survey a small area which one of the most important operation for setting up the plane table is
explain: Radiation is the simplest method of plane tabling, where points are located by drawing rays from a single station; it is most suitable for small, open areas.

q: 25. In Indian tangent clinometer is associated with .............
explain: The Indian tangent clinometer is used primarily in Plane Table surveying to determine the elevations of points by measuring vertical angles.

q: 26. The instrument used for accurate centering in plane table survey is .............
explain: A plumbing fork (U-frame) with a plumb bob is used to center the point on the paper exactly over the station on the ground.

q: 27. The method of surveying in which field work and plotting work are done simultaneously, is called
explain: As established, plane table surveying is the unique method where field observation and plotting proceed together, simultaneously.

q: 28. In plane tabling, the instrument used to measure horizontal and vertical distances directly, is known as
explain: As noted earlier, a telescopic alidade, fitted with stadia hairs, allows both horizontal and vertical distances to be measured directly in plane table surveying.

q: 29. The operation of turning the table so that all the lines on the paper are parallel to the corresponding lines on the ground, is called
explain: As defined earlier, this act of aligning the plane table so that plotted lines are parallel to the corresponding ground lines is called orientation.

q: 30. The plotting of small areas which can be commanded from a single station, is usually done on the plane table by the method of
explain: When a small area can be entirely observed and measured from one single station, the method of radiation is used to plot all the points directly from that station.

q: 31. The method of intersection in plane tabling is commonly used for
options: locating the distant and inaccessible points
locating the points which may be used subsequently as the instrument stations
explain: Intersection is a versatile method used to locate distant/inaccessible points, broken boundary details, and even future instrument stations, so all the listed uses apply.

q: 32. The method of plane tabling commonly used for establishing the instrument stations only, is a
explain: Resection is specifically used to locate/establish the plane table's own instrument station with reference to already plotted points.

q: 33. Spirit level in plane table is used for
explain: The spirit level fitted to (or used with) a plane table is specifically used to check and set the table perfectly horizontal, i.e., for levelling the table.

q: 34. The types of survey in which field work and plotting proceeds simultaneously
explain: Plane table surveying is unique because the map is drawn in the field while the observations are being made.

q: 35. Plotting of inaccessible points on a plane table, is done by .............
explain: The intersection method allows the surveyor to plot a point by sighting it from two different stations without actually traveling to the point.

q: 36. Plane table surveying is graphical method of surveying in which
options: field work and plotting proceeds simultaneously
plotting is done later while records are taken in field book
explain: The primary advantage of plane table surveying is that the map is prepared in the field directly, eliminating the need for a separate field book.

q: 37. Locating the position of plane table station with reference to three known points, is known as .............
explain: The three-point problem is a resection technique used to find the location of the instrument station by sighting three known mapped points.

q: 38. Setting up the plane table consists of operations
explain: Basic setup involves getting the board horizontal (levelling) and placing the plotted point exactly over the ground station (centering).

q: 39. The 'fix' of a plane table from three known points, is good, if .............
options: either the right or left station is nearest
explain: A good 'fix' in a three-point problem is achieved when the middle station is closer to the instrument than the other two points.

q: 40. Plane table survey is considered good as compared to other survey since
options: chances to missing details are less
explain: Since plotting happens while looking at the actual terrain, the surveyor is much less likely to omit important features.

q: 41. A disadvantage of plane table survey is
options: It is heavy, cumbersome and awkward to carry
It can't be used in wet climate
details may not be available while redrawing to a different scale
accessories are likely to be lost
explain: The large board and tripod make it physically more difficult to transport compared to a compass or a simple level.

q: 42. Placing the table over the station such that the station plotted on sheet is exactly above the corresponding station on the ground is
explain: Centering ensures the vertical axis of the plotted point and the ground station are aligned.

q: 43. Orientation is the operation of keeping the table at successive stations such that
options: the position of the table at the station is parallel to the position it occupied at the previous station
the position of station plotted on sheet is exactly above the corresponding station on ground
the table is brought in a horizontal plane
explain: Orientation ensures that every line on the paper remains parallel to its corresponding line on the ground.

q: 44. The method of plane tabling generally adopted to obtain details and plotting inaccessible points is
explain: Intersection plots points by the crossing of rays from two different stations, which is ideal for points that cannot be reached to measure distance.

q: 45. In the intersection method of plane tabling the number of stations needed to be set up are
explain: At least two known stations are required to create the intersecting rays for a single point.

q: 46. Resection is the method employed for
explain: Resection is specifically used to establish the location of the plane table on the map by observing known points.

q: 47. The two point problem is
options: a case of resection method where no ray is required to be drawn from the proceeding station to the instrument station
locating the position of plane table by means of two visible well defined points
explain: It is a resection technique where the table is oriented and located using two known points, often involving an auxiliary station.

q: 48. The size of plane table is
explain: A standard plane table used in surveying is typically about 600 mm x 750 mm in size, as given by this text.

q: 49. The two- point problem as compared to the three point problem is
explain: The two-point problem involves more steps and temporary setups compared to the three-point problem.

q: 50. The three point problem can be solved by
explain: Several methods exist to solve the three-point problem, including Lehmann's (trial and error) and Bessel's (graphical).
